heath_proof: Let a rational straight line A be set out, and BG commensurable in length with it; therefore BG is also rational. Let two numbers DF, FE be set out such that the whole DE has not to either of the numbers DF, EF the ratio which a square number has to a square number. Let it be contrived that, as DE is to EF, so is the square on BG to the square on GC; [X. 6] therefore the square on BG is commensurable with the square on GC. [X. 6] But the square on BG is rational; therefore the square on GC is also rational; therefore GC is rational. Now, since DE has not to EF the ratio which a square number has to a square number, therefore neither has the square on BG to the square on GC the ratio which a square number has to a square number; therefore BG is incommensurable in length with GC. [X. 9] And both are rational; therefore BG, GC are rational straight lines commensurable in square only; therefore BC is an apotome. [X. 73] Now let the square on H be that by which the square on BG is greater than the square on GC. Since then, as DE is to EF, so is the square on BG to the square on GC, therefore also, convertendo, as ED is to DF, so is the square on GB to the square on H. [v. 19] But ED has not to DF the ratio which a square number has to a square number; therefore neither has the square on GB to the square on H the ratio which a square number has to a square number; therefore BG is incommensurable in length with H. [X. 9] And the square on BG is greater than the square on GC by the square on H; therefore the square on BG is greater than the square on GC by the square on a straight line incommensurable with BG. And the whole BG is commensurable in length with the rational straight line A set out. Therefore BC is a fourth apotome. [X. Deff. III. 4] Therefore the fourth apotome has been found.

10.88
**Statement:** To find the fourth apotome.

**Step 1.** Let a rational straight line E be set out, and let BG be a straight line commensurable in length with E; then BG is also rational [D10.1.3].

**Step 2.** By Proposition 10.30, find two rational straight lines BG and DG that are commensurable in square only, such that the square on BG is greater than the square on DG by the square on a straight line incommensurable in length with BG [10.30].

**Step 3.** Since BG and DG are rational and commensurable in square only, their difference BG - DG is an apotome [10.73]. Let this apotome be denoted AB, so that AB = BG - DG, where BG is the whole and DG is the annex.

**Step 4.** Since BG and DG are commensurable in square only, they are incommensurable in length [D10.1.1]. Since DG is rational (being commensurable in square with the rational line BG), DG is incommensurable in length with BG. Since BG is commensurable in length with E, and DG is incommensurable in length with BG, then DG is incommensurable in length with E [10.13].

**Step 5.** Now, BG is commensurable in length with E, which is the rational straight line set out, so the whole BG is commensurable in length with the rational straight line set out [D10.1.3].

**Step 6.** By construction in Step 2, the square on BG is greater than the square on DG by the square on a straight line incommensurable in length with BG [10.30].

**Step 7.** By Definition D10.3.4, since AB is an apotome with whole BG and annex DG, and the square on the whole BG is greater than the square on the annex DG by the square on a straight line incommensurable in length with the whole BG, and the whole BG is commensurable in length with the rational straight line E set out, the apotome AB is a fourth apotome [D10.3.4].

**Step 8.** Therefore the fourth apotome AB has been found. Q.E.F.
